content.title: The Page Is a Data Structure
content.hook: In the previous module, JavaScript lived mostly as a language: values, decisions, loops, functions, arrays, and objects.
content.context:
Now put that language inside a browser page.

The page is no longer just text sitting in a file. The browser reads the HTML and builds a live structure representing the document. JavaScript can look at that structure, find parts of it, and change parts of it.
goals: Understand that the browser turns HTML into a live document structure that JavaScript can inspect and change.

content.title: A useful first picture
content.text:
Think of the page like a tree. A document can contain a main heading, then a paragraph, then a list. The browser represents those relationships as a structure of objects. For example: ```html

Profile

Welcome, Ada.

``` The `main` element contains the `h1` and `p` elements. The paragraph is inside the main element. Those relationships matter because JavaScript can navigate this structure.

content.question: What is JavaScript interacting with when it changes the text of a paragraph already displayed in the page?

options.text: Only the text file stored on the server

feedback.correct: Correct answer: B. The browser's live document structure
feedback.incorrect: Correct answer: B. The browser's live document structure

content.title: What the browser builds
content.text:
The browser takes the HTML document and creates a live representation commonly called the **DOM**, short for **Document Object Model**.

You do not need to memorize the full browser implementation. For now, use this mental model:

**HTML gives the browser a document to build. The browser builds the DOM. JavaScript can inspect and change that DOM.**

content.title: Tiny observation
content.text:
Start with: ```html

Hello.

``` Then imagine JavaScript changes the paragraph text to `Hello, Ada.` The HTML file on disk has not magically rewritten itself. The browser's current page changed. That distinction will matter whenever a page appears to change without a new document being loaded.

content.question: Which sentence is the most accurate?

options.text: The DOM is the same thing as the original HTML file.
The DOM is the browser's live document structure that JavaScript can inspect and change.
The DOM is only the page's CSS.
The DOM is the internet connection.

feedback.correct: Correct answer: B. The DOM is the browser's live document structure that JavaScript can inspect and change.
feedback.incorrect: Correct answer: B. The DOM is the browser's live document structure that JavaScript can inspect and change.
